title: 3 New Anime to Watch If You Miss 90s Anime
content:
1990s was the greatest decade for the anime industry, as it introduced several iconic films and series that are still loved even now. The animation styles were distinctive, and the music was unforgettable, which made them even more memorable. However, it’s not just the plot or aesthetic visuals that make these series special, as fans often have an emotional attachment to some of their childhood favorites. It was an era before streaming platforms became popular, and several Japanese anime series were made accessible worldwide on TV channels in English-dubbed formats. Anime is now a mainstream form of media, pulling in more viewers over the years. However, most beginners are often drawn to the trending modern series that take over social media discussions.

Since it can be overwhelming to find the right anime to start with, many beginners would turn to a series that recently went popular. Needless to say, while these newer series are always a good choice for anyone to start their anime journey with, there are also a bunch of older classics that are relevant to this day.

3) Lazarus

In MAPPA’s Lazarus , three years after the distribution of a miracle drug called Hapna, its creator, Dr. Skinner, reveals that it will kill everyone who took it over time. The first wave of deaths is only a month away, so it falls onto Lazarus, a covert team of former criminals assembled by the government, to track down Skinner for a cure to Hapna before humanity goes extinct. As the first new Shinichiro Watanabe project in six years and one that clearly played into Cowboy Bebop ’s iconic aesthetic, there was plenty of hype for Lazarus ’ premiere, and it initially seemed to live up to that hype. That was short-lived, however, as between the poor pacing and its lack of urgency, terrible English dub, and often nonsensical story decisions, Lazarus ultimately failed to do anything other than look good, and it’s hard to see it as anything other than Watanabe’s worst anime, by far.

2) Goodbye, Lara

The story tells a reimagined version of a fairy tale with striking visuals and a promising plot. A long time ago, a mermaid princess named Lara was raised with love by her father, the king of the sea, and her sisters. However, one day, Lara fell in love with a human prince who lived on land and yearned for him despite knowing it was a forbidden love. Falling in love with a human was not allowed in the world of mermaids, especially for a sheltered princess like her. Still, Lara journeyed to the surface world to meet him. She became human thanks to the potion given to her by the mysterious witch Grace, but it came at a steep price. Should Lara fail to find her true love, she would turn into foam and vanish into the sea. As her wish to find the man went unfulfilled, the potion took her life, and she vanished forever. However, two hundred years later, the mermaid princess is reborn in Lake Biwa and embarks on yet another journey to find her true love. Unlike last time, Lara isn’t alone and has more than enough she could ask for.

1) Dorohedoro

The story is set in an urban fantasy world where a dark and dangerous district called the Hole exists, where the strong prey on the weak. In a world where only the survival of the fittest matters, death is a daily occurrence, befitting the name of the area. The district is also a testing ground for sorcerers who take advantage of the lawless crowd and think of them as nothing more than insects. They perform experiments on those around the Hole’s hospital on a daily basis. Caiman, a half-reptile, half-man, is one such victim of such experiments, as he is cursed with his appearance and tormented by nightmares. He hunts magic users using a trusted pair of bayonets and his immunity to magic in order to find a clue to reverting to his original form. Accompanied by his female companion, Nikaido, Caiman discovers the dark secrets lingering in the alleys of the Hole while also uncovering what transpired in his past.

Do you agree with our picks – or have an anime in mind that you want to add here? Share your recommendations in the comments below.

title: 12 Years Ago, Naruto Reached Its Controversial Ending & It Isn’t As Bad As You Remember
content:
The legacy of the Shonen Big Three remains unmatched even though several years have passed since their debut. As the new era of the anime and manga industry began with shorter and seasonal series, fans appreciate the older generation even more with long-running stories and captivating plots. As one of the biggest Shonen classics, Naruto ‘s influence is unmatched even now. Written and illustrated by Masashi Kishimoto, Naruto became one of the most successful anime and manga franchises of all time. The story of an underdog winning the hearts of those around him and climbing to the top still inspires others.

Naruto raised an entire generation of anime fans who followed the protagonist’s journey from the beginning to the end. However, as a long-running show, it’s impossible for Naruto to be flawless. Due to years of broadcast, the anime suffered from pacing issues and inconsistent animation. Not only that, but since the manga was also serialized weekly, the anime had to release several filler episodes in between. However, apart from this, the manga also received heat for a number of reasons. It reached its controversial finale on November 10th, 2014, but luckily stood the test of time as it remains one of the most iconic Shonen Jump series in history.

Naruto Still Gets Heat For the Unresolved Plot Holes and the Final Villain

There’s no denying that the story had multiple issues throughout its run, including plot holes and the final villain. While the controversy has significantly died down over the years, certain aspects of the story are still criticized. Naruto still causes confusion with many unresolved storylines and unanswered questions. Hashirama’s fate is so famously overlooked in the story that many fans just convinced themselves that the character was so powerful, it was impossible to write how he died. Regardless, a legendary character like him deserved a better ending than fans having to guess what really happened to him. However, that’s just one example, but there are several instances where the story failed to answer major questions, including the power systems and many other plot points.

Whether it was Itachi’s illness or Orochimaru’s sudden change of heart, a lot of the things could be explored better. The final stretch of the story in particular felt rushed with so many things happening all at once. There’s really no way to sugarcoat that the final villain is still one of the most divisive moments in anime history. After hyping Madara Uchiha as the finale villain of the story, he turned out to be nothing more than a puppet of Black Zetsu. Madara’s actions were guided by Zetsu in order to free Kaguya Otsutsuki from the eternal prison her sons put her into centuries ago.

Even now, the ending often receives mixed reactions, especially in the manga that doesn’t feature an epilogue after the final war. Kaguya’s last-minute appearance shifted the flow of the story when it was just reaching its finale. With Obito joining Naruto’s side and Madara regretting his decisions, they became victims of Zetsu despite the war they started and the countless lives they took. Not to mention that Kaguya’s appearance happened with zero narrative buildup, and it seemed more like a quick way to set up the story of a sequel rather than ending the main story when it should have.

Naruto Stood the Test of Time Thanks to Its Unique and Complex Storytelling

Naruto ‘s ending is now viewed more favorably after more than a decade since the plot twist of the final villain was used as a major plot point in the sequel spin-off. The major plot twist in the final stretch of the story focused on world-building and introduced sci-fi lore to ensure the series’ longevity. Additionally, fans also pointed out how this was foreshadowed much earlier in the story, so it wasn’t something Kishimoto decided out of nowhere. Not to mention that there’s a huge change in perception when someone reads a series weekly compared to binging. Not to mention that the anime adaptation stretched out a lot of scenes and even added an epilogue, with novel adaptations that solved the problem of the rushed ending. It focused on most of the major characters and the aftermath of the war as the years went by.

Do you think Naruto’s ending deserves the criticism it received, or has it aged better now that enough time has passed? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

title: Kodansha Launches 1999Tokoyo Building Horror Game on Steam
content:
Kodansha Game Lab launched the 1999Tokoyo Building game for PC via Steam on Monday.

1999. The protagonist, a boy named Akira, finds himself lost in the TOKOYO Building—an indoor amusement park filled with secrets and eerie rumors. There, he begins living and working alongside its peculiar staff, but... did you know? People disappear in the TOKOYO Building.

The single-player game features point-and-click gameplay, low-poly graphic backgrounds, visual novel dialogue segments, and Live2D graphics. A demo is available for download, and the game supports Japanese, English, and Simplified Chinese.

Yasuhiro Nakashima ( Roger ) composes the music for the game.

title: Mameshiba Characters Get Oyatsushiba Spinoff Short Net Anime
content:
Kim Sukwon's Mameshiba character franchise is inspiring a spinoff short net anime titled Oyatsushiba that will premiere on YouTube on Friday, November 14 at 6:00 p.m. (4:00 a.m. EST). There are 20 weekly episodes, each about one minute long, in what the staff describes as the "first batch" for Oyatsushiba . KaKa Creation 's KaKa Technology Studio is animating this "bean trivia x sweet comedy."

Mameshiba (literally, "bean-shiba") are mysterious creatures that are not quite beans nor Shiba dogs, but something in between. Each character sports a different piece of trivia, which is also part of the pun (the Japanese word for trivia is "mamechishiki"). The popular Mameshiba brand characters began starring in a series of animated television shorts in Japan in 2008. Dentsu brought the characters to the United States in 2009.

The characters in Oyatsushiba are in the shape of snacks ("oyatsu" in Japanese), and each will similarly feature their own trivia.

The anime's cast includes:

• Akari Kitō as Daifuku Shiba (inspired by sweet bean rice cake, center front in image above)

• Honoka Inoue as Ichigo Daifuku Shiba (strawberry rice cake, right front)

• Natsuki Hanae as Mame Daifuku Shiba (whole-bean rice cake, left front)

• Miku Itō as Matcha Daifuku Shiba (green tea rice cake, far left back)

• Takuma Nagatsuka as Yaki Daifuku Shiba (toasted rice cake, far right back)

• Kotone Izumi as Ohagi Shiba (red bean rice cake, center right back)

• Yumiri Hanamori as Sakura Ohagi Shiba (cherry rice cake, center left back)

Content creator duo MofMofMo is creating the music for the anime.

Viz Media released the Mameshiba: On the Loose! and Mameshiba: We Could Be Heroes graphic novels, as well as the Meet Mameshiba character guide in North America.
author: ANN

title: Spy×Family Anime Gets 4th Season, Theatrical Film in 2027
content:
The staff for the Spy×Family anime announced on Sunday the anime is receiving a fourth season as well as a new film in theaters in Japan in 2027. The staff also revealed a visual for the fourth season:

The first anime season's first half premiered in April 2022, and the second half premiered in October 2022. The anime's second season premiered in October 2023 and aired for 12 episodes. The third season premiered in October 2025 and had 13 episodes.

The SPY×FAMILY Code: White anime film opened in Japan in December 2023 and topped the Japanese box office in its first weekend. The film is an all-new work with an original story. Crunchyroll opened the film in North America in April 2024.

Viz Media is publishing Tatsuya Endō 's original and ongoing manga in English, and it describes the story:

Master spy Twilight is the best at what he does when it comes to going undercover on dangerous missions in the name of a better world. But when he receives the ultimate impossible assignment—get married and have a kid—he may finally be in over his head! Not one to depend on others, Twilight has his work cut out for him procuring both a wife and a child for his mission to infiltrate an elite private school. What he doesn't know is that the wife he's chosen is an assassin and the child he's adopted is a telepath!

Tatsuya Endō launched the manga on Shonen Jump+ in March 2019. Shueisha published the manga's 18th compiled book volume on November 4.

Shueisha is simultaneously releasing the manga in English on its MANGA Plus service. Viz Media added the manga to its app as part of its Shonen Jump subscription in September 2019. The company is also publishing the manga in print.

The first SPY×FAMILY stage musical adaptation ran in March-May 2023. The second stage musical ran from September to December 2025.

The Nagoya run of the first musical streamed outside of Japan with English subtitles on July 6.

SPY×FAMILY 2: Bakudan Inu-hen & Gōka Kyakusen-hen ( SPY×FAMILY 2: Doggy Bomb Arc & Luxury Cruise Ship Arc), the sequel stage musical adapting the respective arcs from the manga, ran from September 22 to October 29 at Tokyo Tatemono Brilllia Hall. The play is running at Hakataza Theater in Fukuoka in November, and will run at the Hyogo Performing Arts Center KOBELCO Main Hall in December, Misono-za in Nagoya in December, and Yamagin Prefectural Hall in Yamagata in December.

title: Tekken 8 Game Streams Roger Jr. Starter Guide
content:
Bandai Namco Entertainment started streaming a starter guide video for Roger Jr., one of the characters for the Tekken 8 fighting game's Season 3 , on Tuesday ahead of the character's early access release on Wednesday.

The character will be available for early access on November 11, and will launch officially on November 16.

Other Season 3 characters include Kunimitsu, Bob, and Yūjirō Hanma, the father of protagonist Baki Hanma from the Baki manga and anime series. Kunimitsu launched on June 2 in Japan and June 1 in the United States. The character launched on Early Access on May 28 in Japan and May 27 in the U.S. Bob was released for early access on August 19, and was officially released on August 24. Yūjirō Hanma will debut in early 2027.

Season 2 added Anna Williams in March 2025, Fahkumram in July 2025, Armor King in October 2025, and Miary Zo in December 2025.

Tekken 8 launched for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam in January 2024.

The game featured the following characters at launch: Jin Kazama, Kazuya Mishima, Nina Williams, Jun Kazama, Paul Phoenix, Marshall Law, King, Lars Alexandersson, Jack-8, Ling Xiaoyu, Asuka Kazama, Leroy Smith, Lili, Hwoarang, Bryan, Azucena, Claudio, Raven, Devil Jin, Lee Chaolan, Alisa Bosconovitch, Victor Chevalier, Reina, Leo, Steve, Dragunov, Feng, Yoshimitsu, Shaheen, KUMA, Panda, Zafina, and Lee Chaolan.

The story of the game takes place nearly six months after Tekken 7 . The Guinness World Records recognize the Tekken franchise as having the longest running narrative in video game history.

Eddy Gordo was added to the game in April 2024 as the first DLC character, followed by Lidia Sobieska in July 2024, and Heihachi Mishima in September 2024. The game added Clive Rosfield, the protagonist of Square Enix 's Final Fantasy XVI game, as a playable character in December 2024.

The Tekken: Bloodline anime series, which follows the storyline of the Tekken 3 fighting game, premiered on Netflix in August 2022.

Tekken 8 game director Kohei Ikeda (also known as Nakatsu) announced on June 1 that he has left Bandai Namco Entertainment , having worked at the company for 20 years. Ikeda was the game director on the fighting games Tekken 7 and Tekken 8 , the producer on the Tekken 3D Prime Edition game, and a designer for Tekken Tag Tournament 2 . He was also a designer and battle effect director on SoulCalibur IV .

title: The Iceblade Sorcerer Shall Rule the World Author Nana Mikoshiba's Original Novel Gets Manga Adaptation on November 17
content:
The official X (formerly Twitter ) account of Kodansha 's Magazine Pocket app announced on Tuesday a manga adaptation of Nana Mikoshiba 's Kasō Slum de Garakuta o Shūri Shiteita Tensei-sha wa Arayuru Majutsu o shi, Sekai Saikō no Majutsu-shi he to Itaru ~Genten Majutsu no Sōzō-sha~ (A Reincarnated Person Repairing Junk in the Slums Learns to "Recreate" Every Kind of Magic, and Becomes the World's Greatest Mage ~Creator of Original Magic) novel, which will launch on November 17. Meguru Kanadome is drawing the manga, and Akari is credited for original character designs.

Mikoshiba launched the story on the Kakuyomu website in June 2025. The story centers on Allen, who gets reincarnated and lives in the slum outskirts of a magical world. He survives by scavenging, selling, and repairing broken magical artifacts. Unknowingly, by repairing magical artifacts, Allen learns the very essence of magic. He eventually becomes known as "the greatest genius mage in history." But with Allen at the center of magic, the abyss of magic begins to open.

Mikoshiba's The Iceblade Sorcerer Shall Rule the World ( Hyōken no Majutsushi ga Sekai wo Suberu - Sekai Saikyō no Majutsushi de Aru Shōnen wa, Majutsu Gakuin ga Nyūgaku Suru ) original story launched on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō (Let's Become Novelists) website in October 2019, and ended in February 2022. The light novel series launched in July 2020, with illustrations by Riko Korie . Kodansha publishes the light novels in print in Japan. The light novels' 10th volume will ship on December 2, and its listing teases a story finale.

Norihito Sasaki 's manga adaptation launched in Kodansha 's Magazine Pocket website in June 2020, and ended in January 2024. The manga's 16th and final compiled book volume shipped in April 2024. Kodansha USA Publishing released the 13th volume in English on June 2.

A Hyōken no Majutsushi ga Sekai wo Suberu II : Sekai Saikyō no Majutsushi de Aru Shōnen wa, Majutsu Gakuin ga Nyūgaku Suru sequel manga launched on May 27. Nao Kagami illustrates the manga and Ishiya Ōgane is in charge of composition. Niconico Manga publishes the manga under Kodansha 's " Suiyōbi no Sirius " label. The first volume shipped on October 8.

The first season of the novels' television anime adaptation premiered in January 2023. Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it aired in Japan, and also streamed an English dub . The second season of the anime premiered on October 8, and is currently ongoing. Crunchyroll is streaming the anime as it airs and is also streaming an English dub .

title: Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX Game Previews Duels, Partners, Multiplayer, Exploration in New Trailer
content:
Konami streamed a new gameplay trailer for its Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX game , an updated version of the 2008 Yu-Gi-Oh! GX Tag Force 3 game, on Tuesday. The trailer previews the duels, partner system, online multiplayer, and town exploration gameplay.

The new version features modern visuals, voice acting, and enhanced Dueling and Tag Dueling with over 3,800 cards. The physical editions for Switch 2 and Switch include three physical Yu-Gi-Oh! Trading Card Game cards: Yubel, Wicked Canon, and Hope for the Future. Preorders for the digital Switch 2 and Switch 2 editions include the same digital cards as well as a Winged Kuriboh Duel Mate for the Yu-Gi-Oh! Master Duel game.

Yu-Gi-Oh! GX Tag Force 3 debuted for PlayStation Portable in Japan in November 2008. The game got releases in Europe and Australia, but not in North America. The Yu-Gi-Oh! GX Tag Force and Yu-Gi-Oh! GX Tag Force 2 games launched for PSP in 2006 and 2007, respectively, and received releases in North America.

The Yu-Gi-Oh! GX anime series premiered in 2004. Cartoon Network began airing the series in 2005, followed by 4Kids TV in 2007, both dubbed in English. Crunchyroll added the anime's first season in August 2015, and also offers its English-dubbed version. The company later added the fourth season in Japanese with English subtitles. The anime is also streaming on other services including Hulu , Disney+ , Amazon Prime Video , and Tubi .

Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monster GX 20th Remaster , a remastered version of the anime, began airing on TV Tokyo in April 2025 to commemorate the anime's 20th anniversary.

title: Dragon Ball Still Has More to Explore With Raditz & The Saiyan Needs a Chance
content:
Redemption is a hallmark of the Dragon Ball franchise, and so many capitalized on their second chances with Raditz being no different. The brother of Goku and the son of Bardock came to Earth with destruction in mind alongside fellow Saiyans, Vegeta and Nappa. His introduction in Dragon Ball Z gave everyone a small glimpse into the ruthless, bloodthirsty Saiyan , but outside of that and a brief cameo in Dragon Ball Super: Broly , there hasn’t been much else canon-wise.

Raditz did get his second appearance in the franchise in Super Dragon Ball Heroes . This Raditz is a multiverse version that never obviously never experienced the events of Z or he’d be non existent. Goku’s brother clearly stepped up his game in this appearance as he turned into a Super Saiyan 3 in his battle with Turles . He’s ultimately defeated, and his particular timeline is eliminated for failing to advance in the Super Space-Time Tournament. It’s a quick but fun cameo for Raditz, but it doesn’t have to be the end either.

Dragon Ball Should Embrace Extra Raditz Storylines

The interesting Raditz arc starts with the aforementioned multiverse. An evil Saiyan turned good is the route that a few original villains/anti-heroes get in the Dragon Ball world like Vegeta, Broly, Bardock, and more. Bardock and Broly gave fans a mostly evil first impression in non-canon material before being brought in as good, canon characters in the recent Dragon Ball Super: Broly film. Raditz is the opposite of those two, however, as he started off evil in the official timeline. But he could take a similar route in another “what if” Dragon Ball world, just like his father did in the Xenoverse .

The multiverse already unveiled one iteration of him in Super Dragon Ball Heroes . There are surely other forms out there, and like Future Trunks, he could be brought into the canon or stay a fun non-canon entity that exists alongside the Evil Saiyan Cumber and the original version of Broly . He showed almost no compassion in his official form. Maybe the newest one can learn from his past mistakes? In fact, the only moment of any true caring that we get from the original Raditz was seeing his surprise when Goku was willing to sacrifice himself in order to defeat him.

Maybe this new Raditz either finds a way to survive the blast or is wished back somehow and changes his ways? He then might leave the Frieza Force and take Goku’s route. It’s clear that other versions were able to obtain some immense power, so he could turn into quite the formidable ally for the Z Fighters if given the chance.

Dragon Ball Continues To Open All Possibilities

This run of recent content for Dragon Ball has a lot of fan service, but it’s also what a lot people are asking for. For a long time, Dragon Ball was extremely selective in what it decided to focus on. The video games allowed fans to dream up all sorts of scenarios, but few came to fruition or were uncanonized. Akira Toriyama created a fantastic series, and he leaned into some of those non-canon stories in Dragon Ball Daima .

Furthermore, Dragon Ball Super and Super Dragon Ball Heroes were products of listening to the fans. They didn’t need to make everything official either. With the latter, they didn’t need a fully thought-out plo t to bring back lots of past Saiyans and variants of others. They just opened the door to more ideas. Raditz might get the next run or Cumber, but the point is that there’s more to explore in the coming years with the franchise. Would you like to see the return of Goku’s brother in a new form? Let us know in the comments.

title: WEBTOON Reports US$9.23 Million in 3rd Quarter of 2026
content:
The company's net loss shrank to US$7.5 million from US$11.1 million a year earlier. WEBTOON said that the improvement came from higher gross profit and an income tax benefit, partially offset by heavier marketing spending and bigger foreign currency losses. Quarterly revenue came in at US$362.8 million, down 4.0% year-over-year.

Advertising was the standout, with advertising revenue jumping 26.2% to US$49.7 million. Paid content, the company's largest business, slipped 3.9% to US$275.5 million, and IP adaptations revenue fell 27.5% to US$37.6 million. The company again blamed the weak Korean won and Japanese yen for the revenue decline. Adjusting for currency fluctuations, revenue grew 0.2%, with paid content in Korea up 23.7%.

Korea and Japan moved in opposite directions. In Korea, monthly active users rose about 4% to 25.6 million, and paying users grew 5.2% to 3.9 million. Average monthly spending per paying user rose 17.6% to US$9.4, lifting Korean revenue 10.8% to US$169.3 million. Japan, WEBTOON 's largest market by revenue, struggled. Monthly active users fell 12.1% to 22.3 million, and paying users dropped 12.9% to 2.0 million. Average spending per paying user slipped 5.8% to US$22.3, and Japanese revenue fell 18% to US$147.3 million. In the rest of the world, active users grew to 111.7 million, but paying users fell 8.0% to 1.6 million. Across all markets, the company counts about 159 million monthly active users. WEBTOON said it will focus on a Japan recovery. President Yongsoo Kim told investors on the earnings call that Japan remains one of the company's biggest growth opportunities, and said WEBTOON plans to invest 10 billion yen (about US$63 million) in Japanese content over the next three years to strengthen its local pipeline.

Kim also pointed to IP expansion and a new app as growth drivers. He cited Remarried Empress, now a live-action series on Disney+ , as a successful example of a story moving from web novel to webcomic, drama and, soon, animation. North American webcomic Mafia Nanny is in development as a Hulu series. A Marvel app, built in collaboration with Disney, launches on November 16 and will gather about 35,000 titles from Marvel, Star Wars , and 20th Century Studios.

For the fourth quarter, WEBTOON expects currency-adjusted revenue growth of 9.0%–12.0%, or US$371–381 million at current exchange rates. That outlook includes revenue from RI Games Holdings Inc., the game developer WEBTOON is investing in, once the second closing of that deal is completed. Founder and CEO Junkoo Kim said the company continued to invest for growth in the third quarter and expects to return to double-digit revenue growth in the fourth.
